title: Interview Handbook — structure-validation reader

profile.description: The position being interviewed for (Back-End, Fullstack, DevOps), owned by one discipline. The interviewer's entry point: it says which skills are required, at which obligation, and what proficiency is expected at each seniority level. Requirements and expectations are two separate facts per (skill, level) — the whole point of the target data model.

relations.why: a profile requires skills per seniority level; the requirement (obligation) and the expectation (proficiency) are separate records with the same key
every candidate is assessed against exactly one profile

actions.constraint: only the profiles of the currently chosen discipline are shown — discipline is a global scope, not a navigation level
obligation and expected proficiency never merge into one string; a not-applicable cell carries no proficiency at all

skill.description: A skill as such, global and discipline-free (SQL, System Design): one name, one description, existing once no matter how many disciplines interview for it. What varies by discipline lives in the card, not here.

relations.why: per discipline the skill may have one card; a skill with no card in the chosen discipline is still listed, marked as such

actions.constraint: the catalog is global; skills without a card in the current discipline stay visible but muted, so the split skill-vs-card is seen rather than explained

card.description: How to interview for one skill in one discipline — the per-(skill, discipline) record. Two jobs in one card: interpret the answers (descriptors, signals, flags) and know what to ask (questions, practical tasks), with topics as the bridge between them.

relations.why: the card is the discipline-specific half of a global skill

actions.constraint: a skill without a card in the chosen discipline shows an explicit no-card state, never an error

candidate.description: A person interviewed against a profile at a target seniority. Their record is the comparison: per skill the expected proficiency from the profile and the actual proficiency the interview showed, closed by a verdict. Deviations in both directions carry equal weight.

relations.why: expected proficiency comes from the profile at the candidate's target seniority — it is never stored on the candidate

actions.constraint: expected and actual are always two columns; the delta names both proficiencies, up and down shown with equal weight

vocabularies.discipline: two instances (.NET, Java) with a name and nothing else a screen would show. It is the global scope every screen reads through — a switcher in the page actions, not a page. Becomes an object the day a discipline carries content of its own (owners, description, health).
vocabularies.seniority: four fixed values (Junior, Middle, Senior, Lead) — the axis of the position. Never an instance to open; never merged with proficiency into one string.
vocabularies.proficiency: four fixed values (Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert) — the axis of skill mastery. Same rule: a scale, not a screen.
vocabularies.obligation: three fixed values (mandatory, optional, not applicable) on a (profile, skill, level) requirement; a cell state, not a thing.
vocabularies.topic: name-only in the first pass, exactly as the target data model stores it. Reopens as an object when topics gain attributes of their own (descriptions, question links).
vocabularies.group: a heading that organises skills inside a discipline's catalog and matrix. No screen shows a group as an instance; reopens if groups ever get owners or descriptions.

openQuestions: Whether the candidate is an external hire or an internal grade assessment decides privacy, verdict shape and integrations — unanswered as of 2026-08-20, does not change this reader's structure.
Interview plans are out of scope of the first pass by the data model's own decision; the actions above deliberately stop at reading and reviewing.
